Summary: Operating and maintaining shipboard electrical generation, switchboards, and distribution networks aboard naval vessels.
Working with three-phase AC power, transformers, and distribution voltages common to industrial and facility electrical systems.
Diagnosing and repairing faults in electrical circuits, wiring, motors, and controls using schematics and test equipment.
Installing, wiring, and troubleshooting electric motors, motor starters, variable-frequency drives, and control circuits.
Inspecting, testing, and maintaining switchgear, circuit breakers, panels, and protective devices in power-distribution equipment.
Maintaining and troubleshooting generators, transfer switches, and standby or prime power-generation equipment.

Working to the National Electrical Code and state licensure standards that govern civilian electrical installation. Military electricians work to shipboard or military standards and typically need NEC study and licensed hours to transition.
Installing and repairing shipboard electrical systems, cabling, and connectors to marine standards in shipbuilding and repair.
Testing, troubleshooting, and repairing shipboard electronic equipment such as radar, communications, and navigation systems.
Maintaining and repairing radar, radio-frequency, antenna, and communications electronics.

Eligibility for or possession of a U.S. government security clearance, common for shipboard combat-systems electronics work and valued by defense-electronics employers. Clearance is granted to individuals, not conferred by a rating.
Operating active and passive sonar systems to detect, analyze, localize, and classify underwater contacts.
Analyzing broadband, narrowband, and other acoustic data for contact classification, target recognition, and acoustic intelligence.
Classifying and evaluating underwater contacts using sonar returns, acoustic signatures, tactical context, and environmental data.
Maintaining, calibrating, testing, troubleshooting, and repairing sonar electronics, underwater surveillance equipment, and associated combat-system test equipment.
Operating or supporting underwater communications and acoustic data-collection systems tied to sonar and undersea mission systems.
Applying environmental, bathythermograph, propagation, and ocean-acoustic context to sonar detection, classification, and system performance.
